summary: Novocure has been denied Food and Drug Administration approval for its device intended to treat non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to the brain. The FDA’s not approvable letter cited uncertainty around the degree of clinical benefit provided by Novocure’s device, Optune Mya, the company said Monday. The system uses low-energy electrical fields to disrupt cancer cells’ ability to grow and divide. The regulator did not raise concerns about the device’s safety profile, Novocure said. The company intends to meet with the FDA to determine if there are other options that would support approval without additional clinical studies.
